mutations.label: WA #830 REVERTED: the name fallback goes, so a record carrying its kind only in the NAME (`validation:ui_flow:landing`) is invisible again. 645 such records in the corpus, 36 runs called 'no UI evidence' while HOLDING ui_flow records (up to 13 each), and the detector feeds `validation_ui_evidence_failed` -- the check with the most gate evaluations of any (3399).

WB `metadata.check` is ignored, so the NAME decides even when the record declares its kind. The name is a FALLBACK by design: a misleading name would otherwise silently reclassify a record that was already correct, and #752 blocks on the resulting counts.

WC the regex loses both boundaries, so `validation:my_ui_flowchart:x` reads as a ui_flow record. A fallback that matches substrings turns unrelated records into UI evidence, which inflates exactly the counts #752 blocks on -- the opposite failure from WA and just as wrong.
WD the regex requires a trailing colon, so a name that ENDS in the kind (`validation:ui_smoke`) is not recovered -- a shape the corpus writes and the narrower of the two boundary errors.

WE the membership check after recovery goes, so any `metadata.check` at all counts as UI evidence -- an api_smoke record included. The recovery and the admission are two separate decisions and this one is what keeps non-UI records out.
